thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty ALERT — auth-validate-prod is reporting widespread JWT validation failures. Spike in 5xx starting ~07:15 UTC. Affected endpoint: /v1/token/validate. Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.com/auth/jwks-issues

pagerduty: PagerDuty: INC-1976543219 fired (critical)

leo (oncall): ack — I'm on it. pulling logs and checking JWKS endpoints now.

incident-bot: If no ack within 3m, will escalate to SRE lead.

maya: seeing a lot of entries like `ERR jwt: kid not found in JWKS` in token-validate logs. Errors started ~07:15 and cluster-wide.

sam: grep from auth-validate logs: `2026-04-12T07:16:02Z ERROR jwt invalid kid "k_2026_04_12" not present in jwks` — looks like tokens signed with a new kid aren't resolvable.

leo (oncall): checking jwks endpoint: `curl -sS https://auth-keys.prod.redwood.com/.well-known/jwks.json` returns only old keys in us-east-1. new kid absent.

tia: did we run a key-rotate job recently? I remember scheduling an automated rotation at 07:10 UTC.

maya: yep, automated key-rotate triggered at 07:15 — maybe propagation didn't finish.

sre-lead: if key rotation published a new signing key before JWKS was published or caches cleared, verifier will reject tokens. Need either to republish previous key or make verifier accept multiple kids.

sam: quick mitigation plan: push a hotfix to auth-keys service to re-add the previous and new kids (ensure old key present) and force cache invalidation on token-validate services. I can prepare a patch now.

leo (oncall): do it. prioritize getting keys back into JWKS quickly; this is causing user logins and API calls to fail.

sam: preparing hotfix branch. deploying to prod (canary) now. deploy command: ```kubectl set image deployment/auth-keys auth-keys=registry.redwood/auth-keys:hotfix-20260412 && kubectl rollout status deploy/auth-keys -n prod```

incident-bot: Deploy started by sam — image registry.redwood/auth-keys:hotfix-20260412. Will notify on rollout status.

maya: telemetry: auth-validate error rate peaked at 12% of requests; regions impacted: us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Top affected customers: AcmeCorp, Nimbus. Some token exchanges return 500, some 401.

leo (oncall): paging @support to prepare customer comms. ops-bot please update status page.

ops-bot: Status page updated: "Partial authentication failures affecting token validation in multiple regions. Engineers are investigating." Incident ref INC-2026-1976543219.

pagerduty: ACK by leo (oncall). escalation canceled.

sam: hotfix rolled to us-east-1; auth-keys now returns jwks containing both previous kid and new kid in us-east-1. rolling to eu-west-1 next.

maya: verified in logs: previously failing tokens now validated in us-east-1. error rate dropped to ~1.2% there.

sam: rollout complete in eu-west-1 as well; all regions show jwks with both keys. forcing cache flush on token-validate instances: `kubectl exec -n prod -it $(kubectl get pods -l app=token-validate -o name | head -n1) -- /bin/sh -c "curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/cache/clear"`

leo (oncall): confirm full recovery metrics.

maya: recovery looks good — global 5xxs back to baseline (~0.1%). Authentication success rate back to normal for majority of traffic.

sre-lead: mitigation confirmed. keep high-fidelity monitoring for 30m. we need a postmortem: root cause appears to be a key-rotation propagation race — key published but JWKS distribution/caches not updated in time.

tia: taking postmortem ownership. I'll draft timeline, assign action items for runbook gaps (add pre-rotation cache flush, staged rollout, and better smoke tests). target: postmortem published within 48h.

maya: support outreach: I'll draft a customer note for AcmeCorp and Nimbus explaining transient token failures and confirming no token compromise.

leo (oncall): handoff to tia for follow-up; I'm going offline in 10m. tia, you're the incident owner.

tia: acknowledged. I'll own follow-ups and coordinate with support, security, and release teams. setting task list.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-1976543219 moved to MONITORING. No active escalation.

sre-lead: :thumbsup: Good work. Add postmortem item to address automation ordering and add an automated end-to-end test that verifies JWKS propagation after rotation.

incident-bot: Incident will be marked RESOLVED if no regressions in monitoring window (30m).

sam: leaving a note: hotfix is temporary. will prepare proper release with tests and a controlled rollout next week.

mia (support): drafted customer messages, waiting for infra sign-off before sending to affected customers.

tia: acknowledged — will review and approve.

leo (oncall): thanks team. closing my loop.

incident-bot: Incident mitigated. Postmortem owner: tia.
